title: Independent verification of machine-learned black-hole spacetimes (AInstein audit)

creators.name: Pluzhnik, Andrey
creators.orcid: PENDING — register at orcid.org before release

description:
An independent audit of the AInstein black-hole search (arXiv:2607.05489), together with the reusable instrument built to perform it.

Instrument. A finite-difference curvature evaluator that shares no code with the system it audits: Ricci and Kretschmann from a metric callable, the Weyl operator and Petrov speciality index, and trapped-surface diagnostics via the areal-radius gradient. Calibrated on analytic Minkowski and Schwarzschild (residual floor ~1e-10 in Schwarzschild coordinates, ~1e-8 in the paper's Penrose plus stereographic coordinates), with deliberately corrupted metrics as negative controls, and a measured precision constraint (float32 storage inflates the residual by 203x, so float64 is mandatory).

Method discipline. Stage statuses are computed by deterministic gates from artifacts with recorded SHA-256 checksums rather than asserted; validation thresholds were derived from a reproduced Schwarzschild baseline, committed and git-tagged before any candidate existed; failed runs are preserved.

Findings. Retraining the committed black-hole configuration and evaluating on hidden points shows that the method reaches its stated targets under independent measurement (vacuum quality comparable to the reproduced baseline, algebraically general Weyl structure with speciality index 2.27-2.55 where a type-D metric reads 1, and a future-trapped region), and that the configuration is seed-unstable: two runs differing only in random seed give hidden-point vacuum residuals of 0.233 and 0.915 against a pre-frozen limit of 0.286. All three properties are explicit training targets of the upstream objective, so these results corroborate the method rather than demonstrating a new exact solution. The authors' own trained checkpoints are not published and were requested; everything here concerns our retrains.

Not peer-reviewed. No qualified relativist has reviewed this work.
notes: Upstream AInstein code is GPL-2.0 (its LICENSE file) while its pyproject.toml declares MIT; the conflict is documented and the upstream checkout is kept isolated from this MIT-licensed repository, with no upstream code copied into it. This deposit contains the verifier, the workbench, proof packs with attestations, and the measured results including failures.
